defect_fixed.name: metric-cost-is-null-while-readings-sit-on-disk
defect_fixed.before: all 24 (then 52) metric rows carried `cost: null`. The token ledger (untracked/tokens/tokens.jsonl) had 575 readings (T746 retroactive backfill). The two records were never joined — a consumer reading model-task-metrics.jsonl saw `cost: null` while the readings sat one directory over. The brief's standing rule ('store facts, derive numbers at report time') was applied to the metrics record but not to the join — the cost ladder had no path from the metric to the ledger.
defect_fixed.after: tools/token-join.py joins on (task_id, model) and writes exactly six fields per metric row: tokens_fresh, tokens_cache_read, tokens_out, tokens_source, trusted, corroborated. 27 of 52 metric rows now carry the readings with trust grades. The cost ladder has a name (the six fields) and a verb (the join).

t746_rulings_implemented.ruling: token, cpu and rss figures are collected but NOT trusted as reliable or repeatable, and must not drive critical decisions (operator 2026-08-23)
t746_rulings_implemented.implemented: every joined row carries `trusted` (True for dispatch-time, False for retro / fallback) and `corroborated` ('none' on dispatch-time, 'run-record' / 'task-only' on fallback). 23 of 27 joined rows are trusted; 4 are untrusted (retro / fallback). The join propagates the grades VERBATIM — never re-grades a reading.

t746_rulings_implemented.ruling: every reading carries a trust grade; no consumer may silently average across grades
t746_rulings_implemented.implemented: tokens_fresh / tokens_cache_read / tokens_out / tokens_source / trusted / corroborated propagate from the ledger through the join. Legacy ledger entries (T558 / T662 era, predating the doctrine) carry no `trusted` field; the join infers from the source (claude-json-envelope / pi-session-jsonl → True; pi-session-jsonl-retro → False) and explicitly records the legacy in the docstring. An explicit `trusted` is never overridden by the inference.

t746_rulings_implemented.ruling: the `pi --provider openrouter` invocation stays; the tooling changes to fit it
t746_rulings_implemented.implemented: the runner's cwd-slug fallback (`_pi_session_fallback_scan`) is the durable fix that makes the tooling fit the dispatch pattern. A lane dispatched with `--provider openrouter` (the operator's preferred pattern) and no `--session` still gets a reading; the source is `pi-session-jsonl-fallback` and the grade is `trusted: false, corroborated: run-record`. Unit tests test_runner.py:TestTokenCapture.test_no_session_* pin the three outcomes (match / no-match / model-conflict).

second_order_finding.claim: 301 of the pre-backfill ledger rows carried `model: null` — the dispatch path that omits the label
second_order_finding.diagnosis: of 2944 ledger rows with `model: null` today, ZERO have a real model provider (claude / ollama / deepseek / openrouter). They are all non-dispatch harness scaffolding: `sh` (2203 — regression scripts), `zig` (339 — builds), `verify-battery` (262 — battery harness), `sleep` (103 — waits), `python3` (13 — helpers), and 7 named regressions. These rows are correctly recorded as `model: null` because they are not model dispatches. **The 301 the brief names is a non-dispatch number, not a dispatch defect.**
